title: Cut a Word Into Palindromes

concept.title: Try every length for the next piece, keep only the good ones
body: To cut a word into pieces that are all palindromes, look at the start of the part that is not cut yet. Try every length for the **next piece**: if the piece is a palindrome, take it, cut the rest recursively, and then remove the piece again. A piece that is not a palindrome is not tried further, so the search never builds a wrong cut.

Every letter alone is a palindrome, so there is always at least one cut (every letter in its own piece). A word of `n` equal letters has `2^(n-1)` cuts: a cut or no cut between any two neighbours. Trying the shorter piece first gives the order used in the statement.

statement: Cut a word into pieces so that every piece is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards). Print all possible cuts. Write the pieces of a cut separated by `|`. Order the cuts by the lengths of their pieces from left to right: a cut with a shorter first piece comes first; if the first pieces are equal, compare the second pieces, and so on.
inputFormat: The only line has the word of lowercase letters.
outputFormat: All cuts, one per line, pieces separated by `|`.

examples.note: The cuts are a|a|b and aa|b.

hints: Try every end for the next piece, from the shortest to the longest.
Go deeper only when the piece is a palindrome.
When the start reaches the end of the word, record the cut.

explanation: At each start position, the function tries pieces from the shortest to the longest, goes deeper only for palindromes, and records the cut when the start reaches the end of the word.
solution.complexity: Time O(2^n * n) in the worst case, space O(n) besides the output.

code.python:
def split(s, start, current, out):
    if start == len(s):
        out.append("|".join(current))
        return
    for end in range(start + 1, len(s) + 1):
        piece = s[start:end]
        if piece == piece[::-1]:
            current.append(piece)
            split(s, end, current, out)
            current.pop()

s = input().strip()

out = []
split(s, 0, [], out)
print("\n".join(out))
